newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures up in sympathy with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures up in sympathy with JGBs.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended Monday's TIFFE day session higher after sharp gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The September contract inherited the benchmark status as its volume has exceeded that of the June contract for two consecutive days.
The volume of the September was 36,722 contracts.
The June ended up 0.04 at 99.36. Its volume was 27,838 contracts.

"Euroyen futures followed JGB futures higher. Setting up short positions doesn't produce good results because the JGB rally shows no signs of abating. The yield curve should flatten further as players continue to buy contracts dated September 1997 and beyond," a brokerage house trader said.
The March JGB futures ended up 0.75 at 126.28.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.360 percent, after falling as low as 2.350 percent, the lowest level for any benchmark cash JGB.
Traders said some foreigners were selling December contracts while buying the March.
JGB and Euroyen futures softened temporarily after a news conference by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita, but the impact was short-lived.
Matsushita said Japan's economic recovery appears to be becoming more solid.
"We thought JGBs would fall more on the BOJ governor's remarks. On the contrary, afternoon trades merely confirmed strong interest in buying on dips," said a brokerage house trader.
Key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.48 percent, unchanged from Friday.
The BOJ refrained from its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 10 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.50 percent. Also, about 10 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.50 percent.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.50 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Friday.
